tests.intent: Required ADB and managed ORDS inputs remain environment-only; missing, unsafe, placeholder or retained secret values stop execution without a success-shaped record.
The browser document and API are served from one attested managed-ORDS origin backed by the target Autonomous Database; local, proxy, replay and dry-run substitutes fail.

The database inventory exactly equals the reviewed 24-object build, contains the pinned runtime assets and redistribution notices, and excludes source maps, stale engine artifacts, tools and private files.
One atomic load replaces the static inventory and Oracle-resident length and SHA-256 checks bind every BLOB to the build manifest before commit.
Every live object has the reviewed MIME and cache policy; long immutable caching is accepted only when the filename digest matches the served bytes.
Anonymous access is limited to DOOM_API, PUBLIC_HEALTH and the dedicated doom.hosted.app routes; the backing table and all administrative surfaces remain unexposed.
Pinned Chromium navigates directly to the hosted ORDS document with one worker, no retries, mocks, route fulfillment, proxy, service worker, skips, errors or redirects.
The hosted client creates a real database-authoritative MLE match and consumes only confirmed, ordered DMD1 transitions without local simulation or prediction.
The moving-input sample contains 300 sequential authoritative tics and 300 byte-unique rendered canvas frames.
The 300-frame browser sample sustains at least 30 FPS and p95 inter-frame time no greater than 33.333 ms on the deployed OCI application.
The browser leaves its match and proves capacity release so a successful gate cannot strand a live game or worker lease.
Every browser request stays on the attested managed-ORDS origin and is classified as database static or Oracle API traffic, with no websocket, redirect, mock or unclassified dependency.
Canonical secret-free evidence binds build, database catalog, live GETs, browser report and network ledger to one run; partial writes and mutation survivors fail closed.
